title: Yell and Treatwell describe a different business
evidence: nap_check.py on the 4 listings you found: Yell still shows the old address (4 Coldharbour Lane, SW9 8PR) and an old number (020 7946 0999). Treatwell uses the name 'Example Skin & Laser Clinic Brixton'. Treatwell is one of the two sources the AI answers cited.
fix: Claim or log in to both listings. On Yell, change the address to 12 Acre Lane, London SW2 5SG and the phone to 020 7946 0123. On Treatwell, change the name to 'Example Skin Clinic', exactly as on your profile and signage.

title: Primary category is 'Medical clinic'; two of three competitors use 'Skin care clinic'
evidence: Your primary is 'Medical clinic' with 'Beauty salon' as secondary. In Maps, Skin Clinic Clapham and Stockwell Skin use 'Skin care clinic' and Brixton Dermatology uses 'Dermatologist'. These three take the top 3 wherever you drop out of it in the acne scar treatment grid.
fix: Change the primary category to 'Skin care clinic'. Remove 'Beauty salon' unless you offer salon services such as nails or hair. Add 'Dermatologist' as a secondary only if a dermatologist sees patients at the clinic.

title: Profile services don't include acne scar treatment or microneedling
evidence: Services listed: 'Facials', 'Laser', 'Consultation'. Two of your three money searches, acne scar treatment and microneedling, aren't named anywhere on the profile.
fix: Add 'Acne scar treatment' and 'Microneedling' as services, each with a two-line description of what it is and that it is done at the Brixton clinic. Rename 'Laser' to the laser treatments you actually do, for example 'Laser skin resurfacing'.

title: Homepage title says 'Home' instead of what you do and where
evidence: Title is 'Example Skin Clinic | Home'. The profile links to this page.
fix: Change the title to 'Skin Clinic in Brixton | Acne Scar Treatment & Microneedling | Example Skin Clinic' and make the main heading say 'Skin clinic in Brixton'. The opening lines should say what you treat and where, in the words patients use.

title: No page for acne scar treatment or microneedling
evidence: The homepage lists 31 treatments with one paragraph each. There is no dedicated page for either money-search treatment, and the profile links to the homepage.
fix: Build one page each for acne scar treatment and microneedling: what it is, who it suits, who carries it out and their qualifications, how many sessions and how long each takes, price guidance, real photos of the room and team, and the address with directions from Brixton station. Put a book button at the top. Then change the profile website link to the acne scar treatment page. Ask your compliance lead to check any claims about results.

title: No LocalBusiness schema on the site
evidence: No LocalBusiness (or MedicalClinic) structured data on the homepage.
fix: Add LocalBusiness schema to the homepage with the name, address and phone exactly as on the profile: Example Skin Clinic, 12 Acre Lane, London SW2 5SG, 020 7946 0123. Use the same name in the footer, without 'Ltd'.

title: Top 3 only within 1 km; patients come from about 3 km away
evidence: 5x5 grid for 'acne scar treatment': top 3 at 4 of 25 points (16%), top 10 at 9 (36%), strong radius 1.0 km. You rank 1st at the clinic but are absent at the corners and most of the outer ring. Skin Clinic Clapham and Brixton Dermatology are top 3 at all 25 points.
fix: Most of this should move with F2, F3 and F5. Alongside them, earn three local mentions that link to the acne scar treatment page: a feature in Brixton or Lambeth local press, a listing with the local business association, and a page from a partner such as a nearby GP, pharmacy or gym. Re-run the same grid after 60 days.

title: 2 new reviews in 90 days against a competitor median of 9
evidence: review_velocity.py: 2 reviews in the last 90 days (0.7 a month), newest 50 days old. Brixton Dermatology got 11 (newest 4 days ago), Skin Clinic Clapham 7. 8 of your last 12 reviews arrived between 8 and 14 July, then stopped.
fix: Set up a routine: an SMS with a one-tap review link as the patient leaves, one email follow-up two or three days later, and a QR code at reception. Aim for about 3 a month, every month. Ask patients to say which treatment they had and that it was in Brixton, without scripting their words.

title: Two review replies confirm the reviewer was a patient
evidence: About a third of reviews have replies. Two say 'thanks for choosing us for your acne treatment', which confirms the reviewer was a patient and names their condition.
fix: Edit those two replies today. Then reply to every review with a warm line that says nothing about the person or their care, for example: 'Thank you for taking the time to leave a review. We're glad you found the team helpful.' and 'Thank you for your feedback. If you'd like to talk about anything, please call us on 020 7946 0123.'

title: No booking link on the profile
evidence: Hours and phone are set; the booking link field is empty.
fix: Add your online booking page as the profile's booking link, or the consultation booking form if bookings go through a consultation first.

title: No prices and the book button is only in the footer
evidence: No prices or price guidance anywhere on the site. The only book button is in the footer, so on a phone a patient has to scroll past 31 treatments to find it.
fix: Put a book button and the phone number at the top of every page, visible on a phone without scrolling. Add 'from' prices or a price range for each treatment, and the consultation fee.

title: 22 photos, mostly stock
evidence: The profile has 22 photos and most are stock images.
fix: Replace the stock images with real photos: the outside and entrance on Acre Lane, reception, each treatment room, and the team. Add a few each month. Before-and-after photos only with the patient's written consent and your compliance lead's sign-off.

title: Named in 0 of 6 AI answers; Brixton Dermatology in 5 of 6
evidence: You asked ChatGPT and Gemini 'best clinic for acne scar treatment in Brixton' three times each. Brixton Dermatology was named 5 times, Skin Clinic Clapham 3, Example Skin Clinic 0. The answers cited a Time Out 'best skin clinics in south London' article and a Treatwell listing page.
fix: After F1, complete the Treatwell listing: acne scar treatment and microneedling listed by name, prices, real photos, and the same description as your profile. Contact the Time Out writer when the article is next updated, with the new treatment pages and your practitioners' credentials. Make sure the treatment pages state plainly what you do, where, for whom and at what price, so an assistant has something to quote.

title: Facebook page has no phone number
evidence: Facebook shows the right name and address but no phone.
